children: Waverly Advisors, a large registered investment advisor firm based in Birmingham, Ala., has acquired Heartwood Wealth Advisors, a Virginia RIA with $1.7 billion in client assets. The deal, announced Tuesday, closed Friday.

Heartwood, based in Richmond, Virginia's capital, is led by partners Steve Clarke, Sid Martin, Ben Gurley, and Wes Kaufman, and includes nine additional staffers, all of whom joined Waverly through the acquisition.

In selling to Waverly Heartwood joins an expanding firm that has been making a series of acquisitions to expand its national footprint. Waverly says it managed $36.5 billion in client assets as of Sept. 25. Like other larger RIA acquirers, it provides incoming advisors with new resources to help them enhance their service model.

"As we considered the next chapter for Heartwood, we were looking to join an organization that shared our values and could help us continue to grow," Gurley says. "Joining Waverly allows us to remain rooted in Richmond while expanding the ways we can serve clients in the years ahead."

The deal is Waverly's 36th acquisition since 2021, when it sold a stake to Wealth Partners Capital Group and HGGC's Aspire Holdings platform. It is the seventh acquisition Waverly has made in 2026, with more to come. "We continue to have a strong acquisition pipeline for the remainder of 2026 and into early 2027," a spokeswoman says, noting that the road map includes expanding into new markets in the Northeast.
Heartwood expands Waverly's presence in Virginia, where it already has an office in Fairfax and is planning to open a new location in Irvington.

Heartwood caters to high-net-worth families and business owners. Heartwood and Waverly say they take a long-term approach to client service and are "grounded in many of the same principles," according to Justin Russell, Waverly's president and CEO. "Those values are reflected in the enduring client relationships and collaborative cultures that define both organizations."

Clarke is a 30-year industry veteran who registered as a broker with Merrill Lynch in 1996 and as an investment advisor the next year. Martin also got his start with Merrill Lynch, registering as a broker and advisor in 1997. Kaufman also began at Merrill Lynch, registering as both a broker and an advisor in 1995.

Gurley first registered as a broker in 2015 with Harris Williams. In 2016, he joined Wells Fargo, where all four of the partners overlapped, with each leaving in 2019, the year they launched Heartwood.
